site.name: Hardik Vohra

about.headline: Engineering with the mindset of a builder, analyst, and team lead.
about.body: I am a Mechanical Engineering undergraduate at NSUT focused on designing high-performance systems that are practical to manufacture, validate, and scale. My work spans chassis design, structural analysis, autonomous simulation, process improvement, and team leadership across national competitions and industrial internships.
focusAreas: CAD and CAE for vehicles, mechanisms, and component systems
Manufacturing optimization using MOST, KAIZEN, and Lean Six Sigma
Technical leadership across ASME, IEEE, motorsports, and robotics teams

experience.title: Summer Intern
experience.summary: Worked on structural detailing, process improvement, and operational analysis in a live water treatment infrastructure environment.
bullets: Generated detailed Bills of Materials from AutoCAD drawings for trusses, purlins, and structural steel components.
Implemented KAIZEN and Lean Six Sigma practices that improved welding efficiency by 20-25% and reduced rework by 30%.
Analyzed hydrodynamic flow of the water treatment system to assess operational performance and reliability.

experience.title: Summer Intern
experience.organization: Maruti Suzuki India Ltd - Quality Control Department
experience.summary: Focused on assembly-line optimization, operator training systems, and manufacturing documentation.
bullets: Applied MOST to optimize Assembly Line-B, reducing fitment time by 27%.
Developed a video-based Work Instruction System for Brezza assembly training.
Designed Suzuki Basic Training Modules covering operator safety, efficiency, and process understanding.

Performed impact and roll-cage FEA in ANSYS to validate critical structural scenarios.
Supported fabrication-ready engineering decisions for race preparation.

Optimized chassis and drivetrain decisions for better strength-to-weight performance.
Built accountability systems for technical reviews, build readiness, and competition preparation.

Performed static structural and thermal analysis in ANSYS.
Refined design decisions around reliability and component behavior.

Explored control-system behavior through autonomous simulation scenarios.
Demonstrated engineering fundamentals of automation in a competition context.

projects.title: Team Titan Strike Robowar

Worked hands-on with packaging and integration constraints inside the robot architecture.
Represented ASME NSUT in a national-level competition environment.

Validated real-time autonomous movement behavior.
